interactions: THEORETICAL INTERACTION: Triptans are 5-HT1B/1D agonists; SSRIs inhibit serotonin reuptake — theoretical risk of serotonin syndrome. FDA advisory (2006) was based on case reports. Large pharmacoepidemiological studies have NOT confirmed increased serotonin syndrome risk at standard doses. AHS and other guidelines do not recommend against co-use. Clinical serotonin syndrome requires triad of neuromuscular abnormality + cognitive changes + autonomic instability. SSRIs may modulate CSD susceptibility via serotonin receptor subtype effects.
warnings: Monitor clinically for serotonin syndrome triad if doses are escalated; safe at current doses (sertraline 50 mg + sumatriptan 50 mg).

output.query: SSRI sertraline migraine trigger unmask CSD threshold predisposition

results.finding: SSRIs can both trigger and prevent migraine depending on serotonin receptor subtype effects; 5-HT2A activation may lower CSD threshold in susceptible individuals. Brief monocular visual phenomena preceding a full aura syndrome are reported in the migraine literature and may represent incomplete visual aura; family history of migraine supports inherited predisposition. Depression is a recognised migraine comorbidity; both conditions require independent management.

output.summary: SSRIs may modulate CSD threshold via serotonergic receptor effects; brief monocular visual flashes may represent incomplete visual aura in individuals with migraine predisposition; depression and migraine are recognised comorbid conditions requiring independent management.

output.query: migraine prevention topiramate erenumab SSRI sertraline drug interactions

results.finding: Topiramate: no interaction with SSRIs; mood stabilising properties may help anxiety/depression comorbidity; Level A for migraine prevention. Erenumab (CGRP antibody): no interaction with SSRIs; 70 mg monthly safe co-administration. Propranolol: no interaction with SSRIs; may cause low mood at higher doses — monitor. Amitriptyline: dual antidepressant/migraine preventive (Level B); caution with SSRI combination (theoretical serotonin risk) but generally acceptable at low doses ≤50 mg.

output.summary: Topiramate or erenumab preferred preventive in SSRI-treated patients; propranolol acceptable; amitriptyline caution at higher doses

avoided_actions.rationale: Head CT is less sensitive than MRI for migraine-relevant structural causes and is not indicated in typical migraine with aura; even when imaging is warranted, MRI is preferred

Routine transthoracic / bubble echocardiogram (PFO screening) is NOT indicated in migraine with aura; PFO-migraine association is controversial and PFO closure does not reduce migraine [Charles_2017]
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated in typical migraine with aura — no role unless cardioembolic stroke is on the differential

patient.history_present_illness:
A 38-year-old Lebanese-Australian woman presented to the neurology outpatient clinic with four similar episodes over the past 3 months. Each episode begins with shimmering, crescent-shaped visual disturbance in the right visual field that expands over approximately 20-25 minutes, often accompanied by tingling of the right side of her lips and chin. After the visual and sensory symptoms resolve, she develops a severe left-sided pulsating headache (8/10) with nausea, photophobia, and phonophobia, lasting 8-12 hours.

She had never experienced similar episodes prior to starting sertraline 50 mg for depression 4 months ago. The first aura episode occurred 2 weeks after starting sertraline. She is concerned about whether the antidepressant caused these episodes. She has a personal history of depression (not previously treated with medication) and anxiety. Her sister also has migraines. She is also taking sumatriptan 50 mg for headaches, which she started 6 weeks ago after the first neurology consult, with good acute effect. She is not on oral contraceptives (divorced, no need for contraception). Non-smoker.

On closer questioning, she reports that her father had similar 'headaches with visual flashing' in his 40s. She also reports that she has experienced mild, brief (5-10 minute) flashes of light in one eye on a few occasions over the past 2-3 years that she dismissed as eye strain — she never consulted about these.
